title: Math Missing Step
summary: Find the prerequisite behind one blocked math step.
user: Adults returning to mathematics for technical study who need to locate the one prerequisite idea blocking a problem without restarting an entire curriculum.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The asker wants to relearn math and asks which earlier experiences and roadmap decisions mattered; replies span forgotten fundamentals and goal-specific pathways.
A 2026 explainer deliberately pauses an ML sequence to rebuild slope from first principles before advancing.

recurrence: The 2025 request and a separate 2026 basic-concept detour show a recurring need to repair a narrowly missing foundation rather than consume a full linear course.
current_workaround: Search YouTube, jump among Khan Academy playlists, restart a textbook chapter, or ask a chatbot for an explanation with uncertain prerequisites.
incumbents_and_gap: Khan Academy, Brilliant, and Math Academy provide broad curricula; they do not offer a transparent, user-authored dependency sketch tied to the exact failed transformation in a problem.
smallest_useful_product: Static interactive tool with a curated algebra-to-calculus prerequisite graph, one diagnostic prompt per node, and printable repair path cards.
success_measure: At least 70% of pilot users identify a three-node-or-shorter repair path and correctly solve a matched transfer problem within 30 minutes.
constraints: Have math educators review content; label diagnostics as guidance rather than diagnosis; use openly licensed examples and accessible MathML rendering.
why_distinct: It finds and repairs a local conceptual gap instead of competing as a complete adaptive math platform.
